lab.name: HOPN Lab
lab.headline: Trustworthy AI under constraint.
lab.question: How do we build AI systems that organizations can trust, audit and afford to run themselves?
lab.intro: HOPN Lab studies AI systems that stay reliable, private and verifiable under real-world constraints: limited compute, no cloud access, sensitive data, regulated domains and physical safety. Our work is organized as three layers (Route, Ground, Assure), one foundation program and one physical-world track.
lab.agendaNote: This page describes our research agenda. Status labels show what is planned, in progress or complete.

why.title: Constraint is the research question
why.text: Frontier labs optimize capability at scale. Few groups own the question of verified deployment under constraint.

why.title: Europe makes constraint a requirement
why.text: GDPR, the EU AI Act and data sovereignty make constraint a requirement, not a weakness.

why.title: Protocols and relationships are public
why.text: We publish our protocols and raw logs, and we disclose our commercial relationships.

programs.name: Route
programs.question: How do we compose many models and providers behind one reliable interface?
programs.direction: Policy-driven routing across cost, latency, privacy and quality
programs.why: AI-Pass is the infrastructure layer the other tracks plug into.
directions: Routing as a learned policy over predicted quality, cost, latency, data sensitivity and jurisdiction.
Provider heterogeneity: schema drift, failure modes and silent model updates.
Sovereignty constraints as first-class routing rules with verifiable enforcement.
Measured modularity: cost of adding a provider and overhead versus direct calls.

programs.name: Ground
programs.question: What does the system know, and how do we prove where it came from?
programs.why: The knowledge graph is a provenance and governance layer, not only a retrieval technique.
directions: Corroboration-gated graph construction.
Selective graph pruning for constrained devices.
GraphRAG versus vector RAG compared on quality per watt and per euro.
Temporal and versioned memory with contradiction detection.
Policy as graph.

programs.name: Assure
programs.question: How do we know each output is good enough, at runtime, before it ships?
programs.direction: Quality orchestration with contracts and service levels
programs.why: Orchestration manages where a request runs. Quality orchestration manages whether the result is good enough, as a control loop. Quality is treated as a managed service level.
directions: Quality contracts: acceptable quality, error cost, abstention rule.
Runtime estimation: verifiers, self-consistency, cross-provider agreement, graph consistency.
Cascades with contracts: cheap model first, escalate below contract, calibrated methods.
Judge reliability and drift monitoring.
Closed learning loop back into Route and Assure.

programs.name: Foundation
programs.question: What quality per watt and per euro is possible when data never leaves the organization?
programs.why: Compute-spectrum efficiency, private retrieval-augmented generation, phone-scale inference, and offline self-learning document extraction.
directions: Compute-spectrum efficiency study across local and private hardware.
Private retrieval-augmented generation when data never leaves the organization.
Phone-scale inference under energy and memory limits.
Offline self-learning document extraction with LoRA.
Reproducible benchmarks across the hardware spectrum, with raw logs.

programs.name: Physical
programs.question: How do Route, Ground and Assure apply where errors have physical consequences?
programs.why: The same Route, Ground, Assure stack where errors have physical consequences. Every claim will name its testbed stage and report sim-to-real gaps.
directions: D1: swarm coordination under degraded conditions.
D2: assurance for learned autonomy (runtime monitors and safety shields).
D3: language and agents as robot interfaces, with verification gates.
D4: assistive robotics with demonstrable safety.

route.name: Routing regret
route.definition: Gap versus an oracle routing policy on the same request set.

route.name: Cost per request
route.definition: Monetary cost of a routed request, including fallbacks.

route.name: Latency overhead
route.definition: Added latency versus a direct provider call.

route.name: Policy-violation rate
route.definition: Share of requests that break a stated routing rule.

route.name: Time to onboard a provider
route.definition: Elapsed time from contract to first routed request.

ground.name: Provenance coverage
ground.definition: Share of graph facts with a cited source.

ground.name: Contradiction rate
ground.definition: Share of facts that conflict with another retained fact.

ground.name: Update cost
ground.definition: Compute and euro cost of a graph refresh.

ground.name: Answer accuracy per unit of graph size
ground.definition: Correct answers relative to nodes retained after pruning.

assure.name: Cost per correct answer
assure.definition: Spend divided by answers that meet the quality contract.

assure.name: Abstention-adjusted accuracy
assure.definition: Accuracy after counting allowed abstentions separately.

assure.name: Calibration error
assure.definition: Gap between estimated quality and adjudicated quality.

assure.name: Escalation rate
assure.definition: Share of requests sent to a stronger model.

assure.name: Time to detect drift
assure.definition: Delay from a distribution shift to an alert.

foundation.name: Quality per watt
foundation.definition: Adjudicated quality divided by energy used.

foundation.name: Quality per euro
foundation.definition: Adjudicated quality divided by monetary cost.

foundation.name: Offline extraction completeness
foundation.definition: Share of required fields recovered without cloud access.

physical.name: Mission completion under injected faults
physical.definition: Share of missions completed after planned faults.

physical.name: Time to re-plan after losing an agent
physical.definition: Seconds from agent loss to a new valid plan.

physical.name: Unsafe-plan interception rate
physical.definition: Share of unsafe plans stopped by the shield.

physical.name: False-block rate
physical.definition: Share of safe plans incorrectly blocked.

evidencePrinciples: Raw logs, protocols and configurations released with every paper.
Commercial relationship disclosed for every study.
Verified Q1 venues only, checked against current indexing.
Reviewer-risk checks before submission: no unverifiable model identifiers, no missing baselines, no marketing framing.
Human-adjudicated samples for any LLM-judge evaluation, with agreement reported.
Statistical guarantees stated with their assumptions.
